title: Judges 16: Samson and Delilah
body:
Read the chapter → [Judges 16](/bible/judges/16)

**[Judges 16:1-3](/bible/judges/16#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/judges/16#v1)</sup> Then went Samson to Gaza, and saw there an harlot, and went in unto her.
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/judges/16#v2)</sup> And it was told the Gazites, saying, Samson is come hither. And they compassed him in, and laid wait for him all night in the gate of the city, and were quiet all the night, saying, In the morning, when it is day, we shall kill him.
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/judges/16#v3)</sup> And Samson lay till midnight, and arose at midnight, and took the doors of the gate of the city, and the two posts, and went away with them, bar and all, and put them upon his shoulders, and carried them up to the top of an hill that is before Hebron.

- Samson went to Gaza, the chief city of the Philistines, and saw there an harlot and went in unto her; once again the whoremongering spirit had hold of this brother.
- It was told the Gazites that Samson was come, and they compassed him in and laid wait for him all night in the gate of the city, quiet all the night, saying, in the morning, when it is day, we shall kill him.
- Samson lay till midnight, arose at midnight, and took the doors of the gate of the city and the two posts, and went away with them, bar and all, upon his shoulders, and carried them up to the top of an hill that is before Hebron. They wanted to wait at the gate for him, so he took the gates.

**[Judges 16:4-5](/bible/judges/16#v4)**

> <sup>[4](/bible/judges/16#v4)</sup> And it came to pass afterward, that he loved a woman in the valley of Sorek, whose name was Delilah.
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/judges/16#v5)</sup> And the lords of the Philistines came up unto her, and said unto her, Entice him, and see wherein his great strength lieth, and by what means we may prevail against him, that we may bind him to afflict him: and we will give thee every one of us eleven hundred pieces of silver.

- Afterward he loved a woman in the valley of Sorek whose name was Delilah; she was seductive and promiscuous, and Samson started leaning on this other heathen woman.
- The lords of the Philistines came up unto her and said, entice him, and see wherein his great strength lieth, and by what means we may prevail against him, that we may bind him to afflict him; and we will give thee every one of us eleven hundred pieces of silver.
- They knew what it took to get to Samson, just as the serpent knew what it took to get to Adam. The scheme never changed: when the devil wants to attack a strong Israelite man, he uses the woman.

**[Judges 16:6-9](/bible/judges/16#v6)**

> <sup>[6](/bible/judges/16#v6)</sup> And Delilah said to Samson, Tell me, I pray thee, wherein thy great strength lieth, and wherewith thou mightest be bound to afflict thee.
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/judges/16#v7)</sup> And Samson said unto her, If they bind me with seven green withs that were never dried, then shall I be weak, and be as another man.
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/judges/16#v8)</sup> Then the lords of the Philistines brought up to her seven green withs which had not been dried, and she bound him with them.
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/judges/16#v9)</sup> Now there were men lying in wait, abiding with her in the chamber. And she said unto him, The Philistines be upon thee, Samson. And he brake the withs, as a thread of tow is broken when it toucheth the fire. So his strength was not known.

- Delilah asked Samson outright, tell me, I pray thee, wherein thy great strength lieth, and wherewith thou mightest be bound to afflict thee. She was literally asking him for the formula to get him killed.
- He told her, if they bind me with seven green withs that were never dried, then shall I be weak and be as another man. The lords of the Philistines brought them up, she bound him, with liers in wait abiding in the chamber, and said, the Philistines be upon thee, Samson.
- He brake the withs as a thread of tow is broken when it toucheth the fire, so his strength was not known. A man of war should have recognized right there that this was a setup, and cut her off, but he stayed.

**[Judges 16:10-12](/bible/judges/16#v10)**

> <sup>[10](/bible/judges/16#v10)</sup> And Delilah said unto Samson, Behold, thou hast mocked me, and told me lies: now tell me, I pray thee, wherewith thou mightest be bound.
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/judges/16#v11)</sup> And he said unto her, If they bind me fast with new ropes that never were occupied, then shall I be weak, and be as another man.
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/judges/16#v12)</sup> Delilah therefore took new ropes, and bound him therewith, and said unto him, The Philistines be upon thee, Samson. And there were liers in wait abiding in the chamber. And he brake them from off his arms like a thread.

- Delilah pressed again: thou hast mocked me and told me lies, now tell me, I pray thee, wherewith thou mightest be bound. Think how backwards that is: she was openly complaining that he would not hand her the way to bind him. His instinct should have been to get away from her, but he stayed.
- He said, if they bind me fast with new ropes that never were occupied, then shall I be weak; but he was playing with her, for he had already burst through new cords in chapter 15.
- Delilah took new ropes and bound him, with liers in wait in the chamber, and said, the Philistines be upon thee, Samson; and he brake them from off his arms like a thread.

**[Judges 16:13-14](/bible/judges/16#v13)**

> <sup>[13](/bible/judges/16#v13)</sup> And Delilah said unto Samson, Hitherto thou hast mocked me, and told me lies: tell me wherewith thou mightest be bound. And he said unto her, If thou weavest the seven locks of my head with the web.
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/judges/16#v14)</sup> And she fastened it with the pin, and said unto him, The Philistines be upon thee, Samson. And he awaked out of his sleep, and went away with the pin of the beam, and with the web.

- She pressed the third time, and he told her, if thou weavest the seven locks of my head with the web. She fastened it with the pin and said, the Philistines be upon thee, Samson; he awaked out of his sleep and went away with the pin of the beam and with the web.
- Three times she had attempted to have his life taken, and he was still dealing with this harlot; it made no sense, but that is the strength of this snare.

**[Judges 16:15-17](/bible/judges/16#v15)**

> <sup>[15](/bible/judges/16#v15)</sup> And she said unto him, How canst thou say, I love thee, when thine heart is not with me? thou hast mocked me these three times, and hast not told me wherein thy great strength lieth.
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/judges/16#v16)</sup> And it came to pass, when she pressed him daily with her words, and urged him, so that his soul was vexed unto death;
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/judges/16#v17)</sup> That he told her all his heart, and said unto her, There hath not come a razor upon mine head; for I have been a Nazarite unto God from my mother’s womb: if I be shaven, then my strength will go from me, and I shall become weak, and be like any other man.

- She said, how canst thou say, I love thee, when thine heart is not with me? and she pressed him daily with her words and urged him, so that his soul was vexed unto death. Day after day she would not let up.
- He told her all his heart, and that is where he messed up: there hath not come a razor upon mine head, for I have been a Nazarite unto God from my mother's womb; if I be shaven, then my strength will go from me, and I shall become weak and be like any other man.
- This is a scriptural example of why a man cannot tell his wife every single thing in his heart. We do not go by the philosophies of men that say your wife is your best friend you tell everything to; we do what the Bible says.

  Precepts:
  - **[Micah 7:5](/bible/micah/7#v5)**
    > <sup>[5](/bible/micah/7#v5)</sup> Trust ye not in a friend, put ye not confidence in a guide: keep the doors of thy mouth from her that lieth in thy bosom.

    Trust ye not in a friend, put ye not confidence in a guide: keep the doors of thy mouth from her that lieth in thy bosom; you cannot share everything on your mind even with the woman you lie down with.

**[Judges 16:18-20](/bible/judges/16#v18)**

> <sup>[18](/bible/judges/16#v18)</sup> And when Delilah saw that he had told her all his heart, she sent and called for the lords of the Philistines, saying, Come up this once, for he hath shewed me all his heart. Then the lords of the Philistines came up unto her, and brought money in their hand.
>
> <sup>[19](/bible/judges/16#v19)</sup> And she made him sleep upon her knees; and she called for a man, and she caused him to shave off the seven locks of his head; and she began to afflict him, and his strength went from him.
>
> <sup>[20](/bible/judges/16#v20)</sup> And she said, The Philistines be upon thee, Samson. And he awoke out of his sleep, and said, I will go out as at other times before, and shake myself. And he wist not that the Lord was departed from him.

- When Delilah saw that he had told her all his heart, she knew she had him, and sent and called for the lords of the Philistines, and they came up and brought the money in their hand.
- She made him sleep upon her knees, and she called for a man and caused him to shave off the seven locks of his head, and she began to afflict him, and his strength went from him.
- She said, the Philistines be upon thee, Samson; and he awoke out of his sleep and said, I will go out as at other times before, and shake myself. And he wist not that the Lord was departed from him. He thought he was going into beast mode like before, but it was over, because he had broken his vow; the hair was shaved from off his head.

**[Judges 16:21-22](/bible/judges/16#v21)**

> <sup>[21](/bible/judges/16#v21)</sup> But the Philistines took him, and put out his eyes, and brought him down to Gaza, and bound him with fetters of brass; and he did grind in the prison house.
>
> <sup>[22](/bible/judges/16#v22)</sup> Howbeit the hair of his head began to grow again after he was shaven.

- The Philistines took him and put out his eyes, brought him down to Gaza, bound him with fetters of brass, and he did grind in the prison house: a blind slave, put on display like an exhibit, the man that had been slaying them now unable even to see.
- Howbeit the hair of his head began to grow again after he was shaven; they did not keep it cut.

**[Judges 16:23-25](/bible/judges/16#v23)**

> <sup>[23](/bible/judges/16#v23)</sup> Then the lords of the Philistines gathered them together for to offer a great sacrifice unto Dagon their god, and to rejoice: for they said, Our god hath delivered Samson our enemy into our hand.
>
> <sup>[24](/bible/judges/16#v24)</sup> And when the people saw him, they praised their god: for they said, Our god hath delivered into our hands our enemy, and the destroyer of our country, which slew many of us.
>
> <sup>[25](/bible/judges/16#v25)</sup> And it came to pass, when their hearts were merry, that they said, Call for Samson, that he may make us sport. And they called for Samson out of the prison house; and he made them sport: and they set him between the pillars.

- The lords of the Philistines gathered together to offer a great sacrifice unto Dagon their god, an idolatrous ritual, and to rejoice, for they said, our god hath delivered Samson our enemy into our hand.
- They gave the praise and the glory to their idol, a devil that had not done a thing. Really it was Samson's own transgression that caused the Most High to allow the Philistines to bind and afflict him; that praise to a fake god did not please the Most High.
- When their hearts were merry, they said, call for Samson, that he may make us sport; and they called for him out of the prison house and set him between the pillars, using the Israelite man for entertainment and mockery while they honoured their idol.

**[Judges 16:26-27](/bible/judges/16#v26)**

> <sup>[26](/bible/judges/16#v26)</sup> And Samson said unto the lad that held him by the hand, Suffer me that I may feel the pillars whereupon the house standeth, that I may lean upon them.
>
> <sup>[27](/bible/judges/16#v27)</sup> Now the house was full of men and women; and all the lords of the Philistines were there; and there were upon the roof about three thousand men and women, that beheld while Samson made sport.

- Samson said unto the lad that held him by the hand, suffer me that I may feel the pillars whereupon the house standeth, that I may lean upon them: the two main pillars that bore up the whole building, one at his right hand and one at his left.
- Now the house was full of men and women, all the lords of the Philistines were there, and there were upon the roof about three thousand men and women that beheld while Samson made sport.

**[Judges 16:28-30](/bible/judges/16#v28)**

> <sup>[28](/bible/judges/16#v28)</sup> And Samson called unto the Lord, and said, O Lord God, remember me, I pray thee, and strengthen me, I pray thee, only this once, O God, that I may be at once avenged of the Philistines for my two eyes.
>
> <sup>[29](/bible/judges/16#v29)</sup> And Samson took hold of the two middle pillars upon which the house stood, and on which it was borne up, of the one with his right hand, and of the other with his left.
>
> <sup>[30](/bible/judges/16#v30)</sup> And Samson said, Let me die with the Philistines. And he bowed himself with all his might; and the house fell upon the lords, and upon all the people that were therein. So the dead which he slew at his death were more than they which he slew in his life.

- Samson called unto the Lord and said, O Lord God, remember me, I pray thee, and strengthen me, I pray thee, only this once, O God, that I may be at once avenged of the Philistines for my two eyes.
- He took hold of the two middle pillars upon which the house stood, of the one with his right hand and of the other with his left, and said, let me die with the Philistines; and he bowed himself with all his might, and the house fell upon the lords and upon all the people that were therein.
- So the dead which he slew at his death were more than they which he slew in his life. Remember [Judges 14:4](/bible/judges/14#v4): the Lord sought an occasion against the Philistines, and even with Samson's failings and flaws the Most High used him as a vessel of vengeance on the heathen who oppressed his people and gave the glory of their victory to a fake god.
- Israel's salvation in scripture is always joined with the destruction of the enemy. The avenging of what has been done to Israel does not come by striving for equality; the righteous justice and judgment is the destruction the Most High brings on the oppressor.

  Precepts:
  - **[Wisdom of Solomon 18:7](/bible/wisdom-of-solomon/18#v7)**
    > <sup>[7](/bible/wisdom-of-solomon/18#v7)</sup> So of thy people was accepted both the salvation of the righteous, and destruction of the enemies.

    Of the Most High's people is accepted both the salvation of the righteous and the destruction of the enemies; the two always go together.

**[Judges 16:31](/bible/judges/16#v31)**

> <sup>[31](/bible/judges/16#v31)</sup> Then his brethren and all the house of his father came down, and took him, and brought him up, and buried him between Zorah and Eshtaol in the buryingplace of Manoah his father. And he judged Israel twenty years.

- His brethren and all the house of his father came down and took him, and brought him up and buried him between Zorah and Eshtaol in the buryingplace of Manoah his father. And he judged Israel twenty years.
